//: Pushing a v* tag IS the release.
it typechecks, builds and signs every platform, verifies the signature, and
publishes a GitHub Release. Nothing else has to be run. Without the rules
below that one push stops for approval, which is the whole reason cutting a
release has had to be done by hand.
The grant is deliberately only that. Pushing a branch, force-pushing
anything, and deleting a tag all still stop and ask. Note the allow syntax
is a PREFIX match, so `git push origin v1.2.3 --force` is not caught by the
deny rules below (they only catch the flag written before the tag). Treat a
published tag as immutable and cut a new version instead.
Not listed, on purpose: mcp__github__actions_run_trigger. Running the
workflow through the API fails with 403 `Resource not accessible by
integration` because the GitHub App has no `actions: write` scope, and that
is set by Anthropic, not by this repository. Allowing it here would look
like a fix and would not be one — the tag push is the route that works.
